name: Nebius Group N.V.
industry: AI Infrastructure / GPU Cloud / Data Center
title: Nebius Group — what was Yandex N.V., reborn as an AI infrastructure company
subtitle: Arkady Volozh's post-Yandex relisting on NASDAQ, $3.7B of cash, 547% Q4 revenue growth, and a 2026 target of $7-9B ARR — how a corporate reorganisation became one of the most aggressive AI-cloud expansion stories of the cycle
abstract: Nebius Group N.V. (NBIS, NASDAQ) is the Netherlands-domiciled successor entity to Yandex N.V., reborn through a 2024 corporate restructuring that separated the Russian operating business from the listed parent and refocused the surviving group on AI infrastructure. Founder and CEO Arkady Volozh — Yandex's CEO between 2000 and 2022 — resumed the chief-executive role in 2024 to lead the transition. FY2025 was an inflection year: Q4 2025 revenue reached $227.7 million (+547% YoY), the core AI cloud segment grew 802% year-over-year, full-year operating cash flow in Q4 alone reached $834 million, and the company exited 2025 with $3.7 billion in cash and annual recurring revenue of $1.25 billion. Net loss for Q4 was $249.6 million as the company aggressively scaled infrastructure: capital expenditures of approximately $2 billion in Q4 went into AI processor purchases and data center build-out, leaving 170 megawatts of power active at year-end against more than 2 gigawatts contracted. FY2026 guidance is the most aggressive in the AI cloud peer set: revenue $3-3.4 billion (roughly 7x FY2025), adjusted EBITDA margin ~40%, capex $16-20 billion, ARR target $7-9 billion with more than half already contracted, and connected power 800 MW-1 GW. The portfolio also includes three smaller branded businesses — Toloka AI (human-data labelling), TripleTen (online tech education), and Avride (autonomous driving) — that operate under separate brands but consolidate into the group. The board is chaired by John Boynton (Yandex co-incubator since 1990, board chairman since 2016) with independent directors Charles Ryan (UFG / Deutsche Bank Russia, Yandex board since 2011 IPO), Kira Radinsky (Diagnostic Robotics CEO, AI-healthcare specialist), Arne Grimme (De Brauw partner, Dutch corporate M&A specialist), and Matthew Weigand (Accel partner, joined August 2025 alongside Nebius's $700M strategic financing from Accel, Nvidia, and Orbis). Elena Bunina (Head of Science and Education) and Ophir Nave (COO, ex-Wachtell and Tel Aviv law professor) hold non-independent executive director seats. The investment proposition compresses a corporate restructuring, a balance-sheet rebuild, a power-and-GPU buildout race against CoreWeave / Lambda / Crusoe / hyperscaler internal capacity, and the strategic question of whether contracted ARR matches the deployed capacity inside the guidance window.
